copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Jordan and Argentina together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Argentina side, by +5.4pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, Argentina comes in 610 points ahead — Jordan at 1530, Argentina at 2140. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Jordan to win at 3%, the draw at 10%, and Argentina to win at 87%. The away side reads 87% on this distribution — the model's central case for Argentina.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Jordan to win at 5%, the draw at 12%, and Argentina to win at 82%. Reading those three numbers as a probability distribution, the market's view is internally consistent. The disagreement with the model is concentrated on the Argentina side — 82% on the market, 87% on the engine, a +5.4pp gap.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Argentina, that haircut lands the model at 86%; the market is at 82%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +4.3pp. We're not arguing the market is broadly wrong; the closing line and the model are in approximate agreement across recent fixtures by Brier score. The claim is narrower: this side specifically reads mispriced.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 37 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Argentina a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +5.4pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.

editorial_citations.quote: Argentina will hope to defend their title from 2022 after following it up with the Copa América in 2024.

copy.summary: On Argentina, the model is +5.4pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 87%; the market reads 82%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: Jordan v Argentina · the model leans Argentina
